checked.comment: Corrupted linear bandit with a finite set that spans R^d, ||x||<=1, values in [-1,1], linear corruption chosen before x_t, regret on θ. Algorithm 1 does not need T, so leaving T out of learner_knows is right.
Stochastic setting with a unique optimal arm. BOTW needs T (f_T = log T, and C_1 depends on T).
Corrupted setting for BOTW, with T known.
Adversarial: ℓ_t may depend on the learner's past actions, so adaptive is right. Regret is measured against ℓ_t.

The hard environment is fixed in advance (stochastic with one switch of θ), so oblivious is valid; nonstationary_switching would be more specific. Bernoulli ±1 observations and ||θ||<=1/4 are recorded.
GeometricHedge.P with John's exploration matches geometric_hedge_p_john.
Matches Theorem 1: every term, high probability, anytime.
Matches Theorem 19. The conditions C<=T and T>=d are used in the proof.
Matches the stochastic part of Theorem 6.
Matches the corrupted part of Theorem 6.
Matches the GeometricHedge.P instantiation in Theorem 6.
Matches Theorem 27. The bound holds with vanishing probability, so realized_regret is right. The probability label high_probability is imperfect, but no vocabulary value fits better.

summary: The extraction is accurate. All main theorems (1, 2, 6, 7, 19, 27) are recorded with the right expressions, sides, probability types and settings, and I found no errors that need correcting. The only debatable choices are small: the lower-bound environment is coded as oblivious adversarial when it is in fact a single-switch stochastic environment, and the vanishing-probability lower bound carries the label high_probability.
